questions.question_text: Which built-in Azure role grants read‑only access to Azure resources?
questions.explanation: According to the Azure documentation, the Reader role provides view‑only permissions for resources, allowing users to read but not modify them.

questions.question_text: Which scope is the highest level at which you can assign a role assignment?
questions.explanation: The Azure RBAC documentation states that role assignments can be made at the management group level, which is higher than subscription, resource group, or individual resource scopes.

questions.question_text: You have a resource group named RG-Apps and assign the Contributor role at the subscription level. Which statement accurately describes the effect?

options.label: A
options.text: The role applies only to resources in RG-Apps.

options.label: B
options.text: The role applies to all resources under the subscription, including RG-Apps.

options.label: C
options.text: The role cannot be assigned at subscription level.

options.label: D
options.text: The role is inherited only by resource groups, not individual resources.

questions.explanation: Role assignments at the subscription scope apply to all resources within that subscription, as described in the Azure RBAC scope hierarchy documentation.

questions.question_text: Which Azure CLI command correctly assigns the Reader role to a user at a specific resource?

options.label: C
options.text: az role assignment create --assignee "user@domain.com" --role Reader --resource-group RG-Test

questions.explanation: The az role assignment create command requires the full resource identifier in the --scope parameter to target a specific resource, as outlined in the Azure CLI role assignment reference.

questions.question_text: What is the least privileged built-in role that can assign the Contributor role to other users at the subscription scope?
questions.explanation: The Azure documentation indicates that the User Access Administrator role is the least privileged built-in role that can assign other roles, including Contributor, at the subscription scope.

questions.question_text: A user has the Reader role at a resource group. Which of the following actions can the user perform?

options.label: A
options.text: Read the resource group's properties and list its resources.

options.label: C
options.text: Modify the role assignment for the resource group.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a new resource within the resource group.

questions.explanation: The Reader role allows viewing and enumerating resources but does not permit deletion, role changes, or creation of new resources, per the Azure RBAC role permissions documentation.

questions.question_text: Which type of Microsoft Entra ID group is supported for role assignment?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID security groups can be used as principal entities for role assignments, as described in the Azure AD documentation.

questions.question_text: When assigning a role at a resource group scope, which statement is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The assignment affects only the resource group and not its child resources.

options.label: B
options.text: The assignment affects the resource group and all resources within it, regardless of individual role assignments.

options.label: C
options.text: Child resources can override the role assignment at the resource group level.

options.label: D
options.text: The assignment is ignored if a more restrictive role is assigned at the resource level.

questions.explanation: According to Azure RBAC documentation, role assignments at a resource group scope cascade to all resources in that group unless overridden by explicit assignments at lower scopes.

questions.question_text: Which built-in role most closely matches a custom role that has permissions to read, write, and delete virtual machines?
questions.explanation: The built-in Virtual Machine Contributor role provides exactly the read, write, and delete permissions for virtual machine resources, matching the custom role's permissions.

questions.question_text: A tenant administrator assigns the Reader role at the management group level. Which statement accurately describes the resulting access?

options.label: A
options.text: The assignment grants read access to all subscriptions under the management group.

options.label: B
options.text: The assignment grants read access only to the management group resource itself.

options.label: C
options.text: The assignment is not allowed because Reader cannot be assigned at management group scope.

options.label: D
options.text: The assignment grants read access to all resources in the tenant, regardless of subscription.

questions.explanation: Management group scope in Azure RBAC allows role assignments that propagate to all subscriptions contained within the management group, as explained in the Azure documentation.
